answer: Every new key posts a bond into a mirror escrow and waits through an exit delay before withdrawing. During the delay, peers can challenge the key's work and the voyage arbiter can slash the bond. A lagoon-flagged set of keys that enter and exit together is treated as a ring. Rapid recycling becomes unprofitable because each cycle locks capital for a full epoch, while long-lived honest agents amortize the same bond. That is the point: N identities must buy N independent proofs, not N free keys.
